PREMISE_UNDER_TEST.as_specified: F(alpha,T) can be computed as a direct exponential sum over raw zero heights with the theta-exact density, with no unfolding step; a readout that never unfolds cannot acquire Phase 3's unfolding artifact.
PREMISE_UNDER_TEST.my_pre_run_reading: This is very likely a SLOT ERROR of the program's dominant kind. Multiplying gamma-differences by the theta-exact density inside the exponent IS unfolding, performed inline. The immunity, if real, belongs to the DENSITY MODEL (analytic, non-fitted theta) and not to the STATISTIC (F(alpha) vs Sigma^2). If so the same immunity already exists in the repo as phase3's sigma2_theta_exact, and F(alpha) adds no conditioning advantage over Sigma^2 at all.
PREMISE_UNDER_TEST.why_this_is_worth_running_anyway: The reading is an argument. B.0/B.2 turn it into a measurement, and the corrected version of the idea (replace FITTED unfolding by ANALYTIC unfolding, then build a curvature-matched bracket) is a real and currently-missing capability.

P-B0-b.if_true_means: F(alpha) is unfolding-DEPENDENT. The spec's B.1 identity claim is false as stated.

P-B2-power.falsifier: if the order-3 path does NOT botch the curvature-matched known answers, then Phase 3's sign flip was not a curvature/unfolding failure and the whole premise of Task B is unmotivated -- report and stop.
P-B2-power.argument_the_falsifier_has_power: Phase 3's own decoy gate PASSED order-3 on FLAT Poisson and FLAT GUE (poisson_ratio_Lmax = 1.023, gue_relerr_max = 0.026). So order-3 is known to be adequate on flat density. Whether it fails once the same decoys are placed on zeta's curvature is genuinely open at seal time -- the flat gate is direct evidence that it might not. This is the exact gap the Phase 3 lesson named, and it has never been measured.

P-B2-slot.statement: Sigma^2 computed through the THETA path will recover the known answers just as well as F(alpha) does.
P-B2-slot.if_true_means: F(alpha) has NO conditioning advantage over Sigma^2. The advantage is theta's. Task B's stated deliverable would then be already present in the repo as phase3's sigma2_theta_exact column, and the correct deliverable becomes the missing CURVATURE-MATCHED BRACKET, not a new statistic.
P-B2-slot.note: This is the prediction I most expect to hold and it is the one that demotes Task B's headline.

P-B5-saturation.statement: The low-gamma long-L plateau in Sigma^2_theta is Berry saturation, and this can be checked INDEPENDENTLY of Sigma^2 by measuring Var[S] on the same block, where S(gamma_j) = j - rvm_N(gamma_j) - mean. Saturation identity: Sigma^2(L -> large) -> 2 Var[S].
P-B5-saturation.numeric: Var[S] on zeros6[:2000] will land in [0.12, 0.16], so that 2*Var[S] lands in [0.24, 0.32] and brackets the observed plateau 0.280-0.285.
P-B5-saturation.falsifier: if 2*Var[S] falls outside [0.20, 0.36], the 'known Berry saturation' attribution for Phase 3's long-L low-gamma region is NOT supported by an independent computation and must revert to CANDIDATE-not-bracket (the Phase 4 catch-#2 shape).
P-B5-saturation.argument_the_falsifier_has_power: Var[S] and Sigma^2 are different functionals of different objects: Var[S] is the variance of the counting-function residual evaluated AT the zeros; Sigma^2(L) is the variance of counts in sliding windows of length L. They coincide only if the saturation identity has actually arrived at this height with this theta truncation. At gamma ~ 14 the smooth term rvm_N(14.13) = 0.449 while the true count is 1, so S is O(1/2) at the bottom of this block -- the asymptotic regime is visibly not established there, and a miss is a live possibility, not a formality.

P-B5-thetacert.statement: Powered replacement for Phase 2's inert theta-cert (register R-003): recompute the theta unfold with the next-order term +1/(48 pi t), and additionally with the EXACT Riemann-Siegel theta (arg Gamma(1/4 + it/2) - (t/2) log pi) via mpmath, then re-read Sigma^2 and Var[S].
P-B5-thetacert.numeric: predicted still inert: |Delta Sigma^2|/Sigma^2 < 1% at every L, and |Delta Var[S]| < 0.005
P-B5-thetacert.why_run_it_if_predicted_inert: R-003 established that the existing cert is inert BY CONSTRUCTION. Demonstrated-inert on a statistic that CAN see the perturbation is a different and stronger object than structurally-inert. It also removes the shared-machinery worry in the specificity note below.

P-B0.reason: an algebraic identity between two ways of writing the same exponent; there is no confound available

P-B2.reason: DECLARED SHARED CONFOUND -- the synthetic battery is placed on zeta's density backbone using rvm_inv, the same machinery the theta unfold uses. A bug in rvm_N/rvm_inv would move the synthetic and the recovery together and would look like success. Mitigation: the known answers (Poisson Sigma^2 = L exactly; GUE = analytic) are fixed OUTSIDE the machinery, so a machinery bug shows up as a miss against a fixed external target, not as a self-consistent pass.

P-B5.reason: DECLARED SHARED CONFOUND -- Var[S] and Sigma^2_theta both consume rvm_N, so agreement is partially self-confirming. Mitigation is P-B5-thetacert: if the exact Riemann-Siegel theta reproduces the asymptotic-theta answer, the shared term is certified rather than assumed. Without that leg, P-B5 agreement would have to be filed as CANDIDATE, not bracket.
